answer: A mechanism that actually bites: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because prism only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, dawn is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any wharf approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
